blocks.text: Two candidates write equally persuasive letters to a Local Government Chairman about a collapsed bridge. One opens "Dear Sir" and closes "Yours sincerely". That single mismatch costs a format mark before the examiner has read a single argument. The format of a formal letter is a checklist, and checklists are free marks.

blocks.markdown: A **formal** or **official letter** is written to someone in their professional capacity — a principal, a commissioner, a manager, an editor. It is a document that may be filed, forwarded and acted upon, so it must identify both parties, state its subject plainly and keep an impersonal tone throughout.

items: **Writer's address** — top right of the page, with no name above it.
**Date** — immediately below the writer's address, written in full: 12 August 2025.
**Recipient's address** — on the left, below the date; give the office and institution, not a nickname.
**Salutation** — *Dear Sir*, *Dear Madam*, or *Dear Mr Okafor* if you know the name.
**Heading** — the subject, underlined or in capitals, immediately after the salutation.
**Body** — three to four paragraphs: purpose, details, request or conclusion.
**Subscription** — *Yours faithfully* or *Yours sincerely*, matched to the salutation.
**Signature and name** — sign, then write your full name in block letters below.

blocks.title: The pairing rule
blocks.text: Unnamed recipient — *Dear Sir*, *Dear Madam*, *Dear Sir or Madam* — closes with **Yours faithfully**. Named recipient — *Dear Mr Okafor*, *Dear Mrs Bello* — closes with **Yours sincerely**. *Yours* always takes a capital Y and never an apostrophe; the second word stays lower case.

rows: I wish to bring to your notice that ...
I should be grateful if you would assist me
I look forward to your response
blocks.caption: Raising the register of a formal letter

blocks.title: Planning a formal letter of complaint
blocks.prompt: Write to the Chairman of your Local Government complaining about a collapsed bridge. Plan the letter before writing.

steps.text: Fix the format first. Your address top right, the date under it, then 'The Chairman, Ikorodu Local Government Council, Lagos State' on the left.
Choose the salutation and lock in its partner. You do not know the Chairman's name, so *Dear Sir* — which commits you to *Yours faithfully*.
Write the heading as a subject line: COLLAPSE OF THE ODOGUNYAN COMMUNITY BRIDGE.
Paragraph one states who you are and why you are writing: a resident of the community reporting that the bridge collapsed on 4 August.
Paragraph two gives the details and the consequences: which roads are cut off, how far children now walk to school, which market has lost its traders.
Paragraph three states the specific action requested and the reason for urgency: repair before the peak of the rains.
Close courteously — 'I look forward to your favourable response' — then *Yours faithfully*, your signature and your full name in block letters.
Reread for register: delete every contraction, every slang word and every vague time reference.

blocks.answer: A four-part plan — identification and purpose, details and consequences, specific request with reason, courteous close — laid out in the fixed formal format with *Dear Sir* paired to *Yours faithfully*.

blocks.title: Three faults examiners see every year
blocks.text: Mismatched salutation and subscription; a missing heading; and a personal tone — *my brother*, *please o*, *abeg* — creeping into an official letter. Each is easy to avoid and each is penalised.

blocks.markdown:
### Register is more than vocabulary

A formal letter also avoids:

- **Contractions**: write *do not*, *cannot*, *I am*
- **Vagueness**: give dates, places and figures
- **Emotive outbursts and threats**: state the problem and the consequence, not your anger
- **Rhetorical questions**: they belong in speeches and articles, not in official correspondence
- **Abbreviations and text-speak**: no *asap*, no *etc.* in the middle of an argument

blocks.title: WAEC and NECO tip
blocks.text: Spend the first ninety seconds laying out the eight format features as an empty skeleton on your answer sheet. You then cannot forget the heading or mismatch the subscription, and you can give the rest of your time to the content, which is where the majority of the marks lie.

points: A formal letter carries two addresses: the writer's on the right and the recipient's on the left.
The heading goes immediately after the salutation and states the subject.
*Dear Sir* pairs with *Yours faithfully*; a named salutation pairs with *Yours sincerely*.
Sign the letter and write your full name in block letters below the signature.
Formal register means no contractions, no slang, no threats and no vagueness.
The body runs to three or four paragraphs: purpose, details, request, courteous close.
